1.title: The Word Made Flesh
1.text: John opens not with a manger but with the eternal Word — who was in the beginning with God, and was God. By him all things were made; in him was life, and the life was the light of men. The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. He came unto his own, and his own received him not; but to as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God. John the Baptist bore witness, pointing all eyes to the Lamb of God which taketh away the sin of the world. The first disciples answer the call: 'Come and see.'

3.title: Born Again — and So Loved
3.text: Nicodemus comes by night, and Christ tells him that except a man be born again — born of water and of the Spirit — he cannot see the kingdom of God. The new birth is a sovereign work, like the wind that bloweth where it listeth. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up — the cross is the cure for sin's bite. Then comes the verse the world cannot exhaust: 'For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.' Faith in him is life; refusal of him is condemnation already.

14.title: I Am the Way
14.text: Christ comforts his troubled disciples with three great promises: a place prepared in his Father's house ('In my Father's house are many mansions'), the gift of the Comforter, and his own peace not as the world gives. To Thomas's question — 'How can we know the way?' — he answers, 'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.' To Philip's plea to see the Father he answers, 'He that hath seen me hath seen the Father.' Greater works will the believer do, because Christ goes to the Father; and whatsoever we ask in his name he will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

15.title: The True Vine
15.text: Christ is the true vine, his Father the husbandman, and his disciples the branches. Apart from him we can do nothing; abiding in him we bear much fruit. Pruning is for fruitfulness, not punishment. He calls them friends, not servants — for he has made known to them all that he heard of his Father. The new commandment is plain: 'Love one another, as I have loved you.' Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. The world will hate them as it hated him; but the Comforter will testify, and so will they.
